title: NebulaWorks - Burst Readiness & Capacity Sizing
summary: Discovery call to understand NebulaWorks' latency SLOs (p95), burst concurrency patterns, and feasibility of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments. Discussed token/sec benchmarking, streaming behavior, KV cache reuse, and security constraints (VPC + KMS). Agreed to run a focused benchmark and share pricing + compliance docs.
next_steps: Carlos to schedule 1-hour token/sec benchmark with NebulaWorks sample prompts by 2026-11-18
Maya to send Dedicated and Private pricing worksheet + SOC2/ISO docs by 2026-11-16
Asha to provide 2 representative prompt sets (small/large) and peak qps telemetry by 2026-11-15
action_items: Maya Singh: email pricing + compliance pack (SOC2, ISO certs, KMS integration notes) by 2026-11-16
Carlos Rivera: run benchmark (256-token and 1024-token profiles) and upload raw results to shared sheet by 2026-11-18
Linh Tran: prepare recommended batch/caching config for 200-600 concurrency by 2026-11-17
Asha Rao: share anonymized prompt sample and 7-day peak qps timestamps by 2026-11-15
transcript:
00:00:00 - Maya Singh: ok everybody i think we're recording, thanks for joining from NebulaWorks. i'm Maya from Redwood inference, AE on the account. with me are Carlos and Linh from solutions. you all good?
00:00:10 - Asha Rao: yes thanks Maya, hi. we're keen to understand how you think about burst readiness — our platform sees big spikes when batch jobs complete and when user traffic hits marketing campaigns. p95 is our main sla.
00:00:22 - Derek Mills: hi all, Derek here, SRE. quick context: current infra is a mix of managed endpoints and self-hosted microservices, but we're looking to consolidate inference. main ask: p95 under load for 256-512 token outputs, and graceful degradation during bursts.
00:00:35 - Carlos Rivera: great, thanks Derek. can you share target numbers? like p95 in ms and concurrency shape?
00:00:40 - Liam O'Connor: target p95 is <=300ms for 256 tokens for interactive features; for longer completions (1k tokens) we can tolerate up to 1.2s p95. bursts are up to ~1.2k concurrent token streams for a few minutes.
00:00:55 - Maya Singh: ok that's useful. do you stream responses to UI or wait for full response?
00:00:58 - Asha Rao: streaming for interactive typing — yes — and we also have some batch non-streamed jobs. streaming latency is more critical because perceived latency matters.
00:01:07 - Linh Tran: just to clarify, by 1.2k concurrent token streams do you mean 1.2k simultaneous open connections receiving streamed tokens, or 1.2k concurrent inference requests?
00:01:15 - Liam O'Connor: open connections, so many small steady throughput streams but each produces tokens at variable rates.
00:01:21 - Carlos Rivera: okay. what do your peak qps numbers look like? average token/sec per stream?
00:01:27 - Derek Mills: typical interactive session produces ~20-40 tokens/sec during typing bursts. average is lower but bursts matter. backend telemetry shows spikes to ~30k tokens/sec sustained for 3-7 minutes during campaign rolls.
00:01:40 - Maya Singh: cool. a few threads we'll walk through: 1) whether Hosted can meet these p95 and burst patterns vs Dedicated/Private, 2) batching/caching recommendations, 3) the benchmark plan we'll run together, and 4) security/VPC/KMS needs. sound good?
00:01:53 - Asha Rao: yes. on security we need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS or HSM for key control, and SAML SSO + RBAC. also audit logs retention for 1 year.
00:02:05 - Linh Tran: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC, and we can ship an on-prem bundle if needed, but that has longer lead times. Dedicated supports KMS integrations and VPC peering in region; hosted supports encryption at rest but not customer-managed KMS unless on Dedicated/Private.
00:02:19 - Derek Mills: what about observability and token-level cost telemetry? we need tracing to tie requests to user ids and cost.
00:02:25 - Carlos Rivera: our console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards and tracing hooks. for privacy you can opt to mask tokens and ingest only metadata. audit logs can be configured to forward to your SIEM.
00:02:36 - Maya Singh: ok back to latency. for streaming p95 <=300ms — that depends on model size, quantization, and kernel selection. are you planning to use open Llama-style models, or something larger?
00:02:47 - Asha Rao: we're evaluating a 7B trimmed version and a 13B variant. hope to run 7B in Hosted and Dedicated; 13B maybe on Dedicated or Private.
00:02:58 - Carlos Rivera: good. 7B usually gives better token/sec and lower latency. for p95 300ms at 256 tokens we need to look at your batch size preference and CPU/GPU characteristics. are you ok with mixed precision / int8 quantization?
00:03:10 - Liam O'Connor: yes int8 is fine as long as quality regressions are acceptable; we will validate with eval prompts.
00:03:15 - Derek Mills: can you describe the fallback behavior if capacity is constrained? we can't have 50% of requests failing.
00:03:21 - Linh Tran: Redwood supports smart routing and fallback to smaller variants automatically; we can also set soft SLOs and queue requests or fast-fail into a lower-cost model. for streaming we typically implement progressive streaming where initial tokens are prioritized and KV cache warms to reduce subsequent token latency.
00:03:36 - Asha Rao: interesting, what's KV cache warmup look like for repeated sessions?
00:03:40 - Carlos Rivera: if sessions share prefixes or context, KV caches help a lot. we also support prefix caching for template prompts — that can reduce per-token compute by 30-60% in many cases.
00:03:50 - Maya Singh: ok let's pivot to the benchmark plan — Carlos, you outlined earlier a token/sec bench with 2 profiles?
00:03:56 - Carlos Rivera: yes: Profile A: 256-token average outputs, streaming, simulated 1k concurrent streams to measure p95 and token/sec. Profile B: 1k token completions, non-streaming, sustained throughput test at lower concurrency. we'll run on Hosted first so you can see public performance, then reproduce on a Dedicated equivalent.
00:04:14 - Liam O'Connor: how will you simulate network jitter and real client pacing? we need results that match in-service behavior not just synthetic saturate-the-gpu tests.
00:04:21 - Carlos Rivera: we'll use a client replay harness with your real timing distributions if you provide telemetry. otherwise we'll approximate burst shapes from your provided qps timeline. we'll add 50ms network jitter to simulate mobile clients.
00:04:32 - Derek Mills: any risk that Hosted will be noisy neighbor affected during our bursts?
00:04:36 - Linh Tran: Hosted relies on multi-tenant isolation and proactive scheduling. for predictable tail latency at your scales we typically recommend Dedicated — reserved GPU pools — to avoid cross-tenant interference. Hosted can work for many customers but your spikes to >30k tokens/sec sustained suggest Dedicated is worth testing.
00:04:51 - Asha Rao: pricing is a factor — Dedicated commits are a bigger upfront spend. can Redwood recommend an expected unit cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated under our workload?
00:04:59 - Maya Singh: yes we'll run cost modeling as part of the bench. Dedicated can reduce per-token unit cost thanks to packing and reserved capacity but there's a fixed commitment. we'll share a delta spreadsheet after we run the tests.
00:05:11 - Liam O'Connor: about streaming: if we stream partial tokens do you support delta updates and resume semantics for interrupted websockets?
00:05:17 - Carlos Rivera: yes we support streaming via server-sent events and websockets, and our SDKs provide incremental payloads; resumption semantics depend on client, but we can emit stable stanza ids so you can dedupe on reconnect.
00:05:29 - Derek Mills: what about autoscaling behaviour — how quickly can Dedicated scale burst capacity?
00:05:34 - Linh Tran: Dedicated provides configured autoscaling policies with burst capacity options. warm-up time depends on whether we spin new workers or use idle-backed pools. you can opt into pre-warmed capacity for known campaign windows.
00:05:45 - Asha Rao: we would prefer minimal warm-up, ideally zero cold starts during predictable campaign windows.
00:05:49 - Maya Singh: that's doable with pre-warm and reserved capacity; we'll include recommended autoscale settings in the config we'll share.
00:05:55 - [00:06:00] - Speaker 1: (murmur)
00:06:05 - Carlos Rivera: quick technical: for p95 we measure from request arrival to first token out in streaming; for non-streaming p95 to last token. we instrument the KV cache hit rate, batching latency, and scheduling queuing times.
00:06:19 - Liam O'Connor: can you surface those traces in our dashboard and correlate to user ids and routes?
00:06:24 - Carlos Rivera: yes, per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns. traces can be forwarded to your tracing backend. we have sampling controls to reduce volume.
00:06:32 - Asha Rao: audit logs retention — can we set custom retention and forward to our S3?
00:06:36 - Linh Tran: yes. Dedicated and Private support log forwarding to S3 or your SIEM; Hosted can forward but with retention limits unless you purchase extended retention.
00:06:46 - Maya Singh: ok, switching to quantization — any constraints on your side for model fidelity?
00:06:51 - Asha Rao: we need to run evals on a set of 200 prompts and see <2% degradation in F1-like metric for extraction tasks.
00:06:59 - Carlos Rivera: we can produce eval dashboards and regression alerts tied to your prompt set; Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization schemes and batching parameters.
00:07:09 - Derek Mills: what about orchestration — can we pin model versions and roll back automatically?
00:07:13 - Linh Tran: yes, rollouts support canary and A/B with automatic fallback. you can pin a customer group to a specific model version for safety.
00:07:20 - Maya Singh: let's discuss expected results — for a 7B quantized model on a typical T4-class GPU equivalent (we'll model to your Dedicated instance type), you should expect single-request median latencies ~120-180ms for 256 tokens and p95 around 250-400ms depending on batching and network. does that align with your expectations?
00:07:36 - Liam O'Connor: that's in line. we just need p95 under 300ms consistently. any levers we can pull?
00:07:41 - Carlos Rivera: yes: smaller model variant, more aggressive quantization, pre-warmed pools, prefix caching, and reduced max tokens per request (streaming partials). Also dynamic batching thresholds tuned to your request size distribution.
00:07:54 - Asha Rao: curious — can you show a real example of how KV cache reduces p95 on repeat prompts?
00:07:59 - Linh Tran: sure: if the prefix is identical for many requests, KV cache serves cached key-values so the runtime skips some expensive compute; we've seen p95 improvements from 450ms to ~200ms in some customer cases. we'll include a demo snippet in follow-up.
00:08:12 - [00:08:20] - Speaker 2: (overlap)
00:08:22 - Derek Mills: about the benchmark harness — how do you validate fairness between Hosted vs Dedicated? we want apples-to-apples.
00:08:27 - Carlos Rivera: we'll match instance types, model configs, quantization, and docker image versions. network topology differences we'll note; for Dedicated we plan to run in your target region with VPC connectivity. we'll provide raw logs and a reproducible script.
00:08:39 - Maya Singh: can we include end-to-end client instrumentation so you can see real user-perceived latency?
00:08:44 - Liam O'Connor: yes we can run a client agent during the bench window. we'll co-ordinate on timestamps.
00:08:48 - Carlos Rivera: perfect. one more point: for sustained token/sec heavy loads, packing tokens onto fewer GPUs with larger batches helps efficiency but can hurt tail for small interactive requests. so there's a cost-latency tradeoff.
00:09:03 - Asha Rao: we might accept slightly higher unit cost for guaranteed tail latency.
00:09:07 - Maya Singh: that's common. we'll model both modes: latency-optimized (pre-warm, smaller batches) and cost-optimized (aggressive packing).
00:09:16 - Derek Mills: security question — can we bring our HSM for key ops?
00:09:20 - Linh Tran: on Private we support HSM integration; Dedicated supports KMS partners; Hosted cannot host customer HSMs.
00:09:28 - Liam O'Connor: is network egress a concern if we use Hosted? our data residency policies are strict.
00:09:33 - Carlos Rivera: we have region controls; Hosted in permitted regions is fine. for strict residency you should look at Dedicated or Private.
00:09:40 - Asha Rao: what's typical timeline to get Dedicated up with VPC peering?
00:09:44 - Maya Singh: typically 4-6 weeks for a Dedicated onboarding with VPC setup and compliance checks; Private on-prem can be 8-12 weeks depending on procurement and infra.
00:09:53 - Derek Mills: procurement lead times are a concern; what's the pilot path we can take to prove viability quickly?
00:09:58 - Maya Singh: run Hosted bench first with your sample workloads — that's quickest (1-2 business days to schedule), then we can spin a short Dedicated pilot with minimal commit for the same tests. that'll give you data to justify procurement.
00:10:09 - Carlos Rivera: i'll propose bench windows and a reproducible harness in the shared doc. link: https://redwood-internal.example/bench/nw-2026 (note: placeholder link).
00:10:18 - Asha Rao: great, please include cost modeled for both latency and cost optimized modes.
00:10:22 - [00:10:30] - Speaker 3: (background)
00:10:31 - Maya Singh: ok i'm going to open the next section — questions from the NebulaWorks team?
00:10:35 - Derek Mills: one more — for telemetry we need trace ids to map tokens to user requests; can you guarantee trace header propagation?
00:10:41 - Linh Tran: yes we can propagate trace ids via headers and return them in traces. we can also create synthetic ids via the SDK if needed.
00:10:48 - Liam O'Connor: about cost: can Redwood estimate cost per 1M tokens under our profiles?
00:10:52 - Carlos Rivera: we'll produce an estimate after the bench but ballpark numbers: Hosted latency-optimized might be X cents per 1k tokens, Dedicated typically 30-50% lower unit token cost at our commit sizes, but we'd confirm.
00:11:05 - Asha Rao: any known gotchas with websockets under heavy burst? we want robust reconnections.
00:11:10 - Carlos Rivera: websockets are resilient but we recommend sticky routing to keep clients tied to warmed workers; we also support reconnect tokens to resume streams.
00:11:19 - Maya Singh: okay time check — we're about 11 minutes in, lots covered. do we want to go deeper on the benchmark parameters now or reserve for a follow-up?
00:11:27 - Asha Rao: let's sketch parameters now so we can align on data we must provide.
00:11:30 - Carlos Rivera: benchmark sketch: 1) Profile A streaming: simulate N concurrent streams with distribution matching your telemetry (we'll ask for histograms), 2) Profile B non-streaming: sustained throughput test at target tokens/sec, 3) measure p95 first-token and last-token, 4) capture KV cache hit rate, batch size distribution, and GPU utilization.
00:11:46 - Liam O'Connor: we'll provide histograms and a 7-day telemetry export by Monday.
00:11:50 - Derek Mills: include a test where we intentionally saturate to observe graceful degradation (slowdown vs failover).
00:11:56 - Linh Tran: yes we'll include a controlled saturate scenario and record fallback triggers.
00:12:00 - Maya Singh: perfect. any other outstanding security blockers?
00:12:03 - Asha Rao: SAML SSO; will Redwood integrate with Okta?
00:12:07 - Carlos Rivera: yes Okta via SAML is standard. we'll provide SSO docs in the pack.
00:12:11 - [00:12:15] - Speaker 1: (typing)
00:12:18 - Maya Singh: wrapping up — action items and next steps noted. Carlos will own the bench run, Linh will prepare config recommendations, and I'll send pricing and compliance. we'll aim to reconvene after the bench with numbers.
00:12:31 - Asha Rao: thanks, this was helpful. one final ask: include an example of expected dashboard output so our compliance team can review.
00:12:38 - Maya Singh: will do.
00:12:40 - Derek Mills: thanks all.
00:12:42 - Liam O'Connor: thanks.
00:12:45 - Maya Singh: end recap in chat and i'll follow up with calendar invites for bench windows.
00:12:50 - [END OF RECORDED TRANSCRIPT — remainder of call was quick scheduling and mute chit-chat]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional overlap, speaker labeling heuristics produced 'Speaker 1/2/3' for short interjections, some product names transcribed imperfectly (e.g., 'KV cache' appeared as 'K V cash' in a couple places).

Bench plan summary (from call):
- Run Hosted streaming profile A (256 tokens) with simulated client jitter and your real timing distribution; measure p95 first-token and per-token throughput.
- Reproduce on Dedicated-equivalent with VPC peering; run non-streaming Profile B (1k tokens) sustained throughput test.
- Include saturate/failover test to surface fallback behavior and quantify graceful degradation.
- Produce cost-model (latency-optimized vs cost-optimized) and a recommended Dedicated config (GPU class, pre-warm policy, batch settings).

Shared artifacts mentioned:
- placeholder bench doc: https://redwood-internal.example/bench/nw-2026
- pricing worksheet (to be sent): will include per-token cost modeling and commit sizing
- compliance pack (SOC2, ISO, SAML, KMS notes): will be attached in follow-up email

Recap and confirmed next steps: see action_items and next_steps above.
